claim: Larger base model capacity better absorbs domain-specific knowledge, leading to higher absolute performance after domain-specific post-training.
falsifier: Train models of varying capacities (e.g., 1B, 8B, 32B) with the same domain-specific post-training pipeline on a fixed domain; measure final performance and verify monotonic improvement with capacity.

exclusions: Evidence is limited to the reported system (Qwen3-based models from 8B to 32B parameters), task (SFC certification exams), and experimental conditions; transfer beyond them is unestablished.

title: Base model capacity–absolute performance after domain-specific principle

conditions: When the reference ratio method is applied under assumptions that are not strictly valid
exclusions: Limited to the theoretical analysis presented; the specific errors depend on the assumptions made

title: Reference ratio method–Approximation quality and need boundary

claim: In quantum annealing, a narrow eigenvalue interval (small dynamic range) leads to random annealing behavior and reduced solvability, while a wide interval allows better processor resolution.
falsifier: The effect of eigenvalue interval width can be tested by constructing QUBO problems with controlled dynamic range and measuring ground state convergence probability on a D-Wave QPU.

conditions: comparison between graph coloring (wide interval) and parallel machine problem (narrow interval)
exclusions: Evidence is limited to the two problem types compared; transfer to other problems with varying dynamic range is unestablished.

title: Eigenvalue interval width–solvability and annealing behavior boundary
